open.verify: Re-extracted binary: X6r def @221921361 is the `..`-after-directory guard (split on `/`, returns true if a `..` segment follows any real directory segment). It is called inside the shared validatePath `Q6r(e,t,r,n)` at occurrence 3 (@221922164, `if(X6r(o))return{...reason:"Path contains '..' traversal after a directory segment..."}`). Confirmed Q6r's three call sites: command positional paths (@225595999), redirect targets `Q6r(o,t,r,"create")` (@225598742, `for(let{target:o}of e){if(o==="/dev/null")continue;...}`), and cd targets `Q6r(n,t,r,"read")` (@225681178). So CC applies X6r to redirect/create-op paths, exactly as claimed. Port: command_path_containment.rs:911 emits the byte-exact message (command-path half DONE). But path_constraints.rs (owns redirect + cd containment) has ZERO references to dotdot_after_directory_segment (grep count 0); its redirect containment (line 645-646) and cd containment (line 689-703) resolve targets via expand_redirect_target/expand_cd_target → filesystem::expand_path → normalize_lexically (filesystem.rs:242-258) which COLLAPSES `..` after a normal segment. Real security-sensitive under-ask (symlink-escape defense bypass) for redirect and cd targets; not an accepted divergence.
